newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: New Zealand yields close lower but off lows.
newsitem.headline: New Zealand yields close lower but off lows.

text.p: New Zealand yields ended five to six basis points lower on Friday but mild selling at the close limited gains.
Dealers attributed the late retracement to profit taking and book squaring ahead of the weekend.
Business is likely to be quiet on Monday with the U.S. on a long weekend for the President's Day holiday.

Yields got a boost from three quarters in the morning -- a muscular U.S. treasuries performace, the rise of the New Zealand dollar Trade-Weighted Index above 69.0 to fresh 8-1/2 year highs, and new eurokiwi activity.

Despite the strength of the TWI, dealers said the bill market's performance was unconvincing. They said the bills should have rallied on after the futures apparently broke technical levels, but the market failed to kick on.
One said that it may need the TWI to sit up above 69 for a couple of days for traders to be convinced of its strength.
Another inhibiting factor is strong funding demand from some banks which are experiencing another surge in demand for home lending.
In the bond market, traders said there was potential for more eurokiwi issues in the two to three year maturities.

New Zealand Food Price Index rose 0.6 percent in January, slightly on the high side of expectations, and dealers said it was yet another economic indicator to show inflationary pressures were far from dead.
